name: Gangavaram
notes: CORRECTED from deck's 21.0m: harbour depth is 20.2m and the port CAN handle 200000 DWT, but the two berths with priority allocation for Coal/Coke (Berth 5 & 6) have official PERMISSIBLE DRAFT 18.0m (designed depth 19.5m), LOA up to 300-320m, displacement cap 236000mt. Official monsoon period is 1-May to 30-Nov (wider than the generic Jun-Sep window this MVP's feasibility.py currently assumes - see README gap). Source: Adani Gangavaram Port BPTS/AGPL/05, w.e.f. 1-Apr-2024, Section B (Berth Parameters) and Definitions.
ops_notes: Monsoon 1 May-30 Nov per Adani Gangavaram berthing policy (cdn.gac.com/prod/docs/INDIA-Gangavaram_New-BPTS-Oct-2024.pdf). Discharge rate is a planning figure set below the port's 48,545 t/24h coking-coal record (in.thedollarbusiness.com) | weather_delay_days_monsoon 1.5: expected days per call lost to swell in the port's monsoon months (open-sea berths lose more than sheltered or river berths) - estimate for planning.
ops_data_confidence: monsoon verified; rate estimate from published record
shore_equipment: 2 grab ship unloaders on two mechanised coal berths (20 mtpa), plus mobile harbour cranes
handling_source: Hellenic Shipping News / GEM wiki (hellenicshippingnews.com/gangavaram-port-achieves-record-in-cargo-handling; gem.wiki/Gangavaram_Port)

name: Dhamra
notes: ~185000t handled; serves Rourkela plant. CAVEAT (2026-09-22): real IMF PortWatch data shows Dhamra's aggregate dry-bulk port-call count does NOT dip in Jun-Sep (+9.9% vs rest of year, see data/imf_portwatch_summary.csv) - doesn't necessarily disprove a Capesize-specific draft restriction (aggregate port calls aren't broken down by vessel size in that dataset), but it's a real data point worth reconciling with this 0.5m figure, which otherwise is unverified beyond the original deck source.
ops_notes: Monsoon 15 May-30 Sep and 50,000+ t/day design rate per Dhamra berthing policy BPTS_DPC_01 (adaniports.com); record 132,365 t in 24h (odishabytes.com) | weather_delay_days_monsoon 1.0: expected days per call lost to swell in the port's monsoon months (open-sea berths lose more than sheltered or river berths) - estimate for planning.
shore_equipment: 5 grab ship unloaders of 2,800 t/h and 2 mobile harbour cranes (LHM 400, 37 m3 grabs)

name: Paradip
notes: CORRECTED (2026-09-22) from the deck's 17.1m: that was a generic depth figure, not specific to the actual coking-coal berth. Real data from paradipport.gov.in's own live 'Berth Specifications' page: Berth No. 3 (New Coal Import Berth), commodity explicitly COKING COAL, LOA 300m, Beam 46m, Draft 16.00m (sailing up to 16.00m during high tide). Capesize (18.0m draft) REMOVED from allowed classes - does not fit even at high tide; this confirms the pre-existing 'Capesize only part-laden' note was directionally right but the port doesn't have a dedicated coking-coal berth deep enough for full Capesize draft at all, laden or not. Post-Panamax (15.0m draft) fits and is kept. Nearby thermal-coal berths (5,6,7,8) are shallower still (14.50m) and not used for this figure since they're not the coking-coal berth. Monsoon reduction (0.8m) is still the original unverified deck figure - not addressed by this source. CAVEAT: same PortWatch cross-check as before - Paradip's aggregate dry-bulk calls run +9.7% in Jun-Sep, no visible aggregate dip, see data/imf_portwatch_summary.csv.
ops_notes: Discharge rate = FY24 average output per ship berth-day, all cargo (constructiontimes.co.in citing Ministry of Ports). Monsoon window not published: Jun-Nov assumed (SW monsoon plus Oct-Nov cyclone peak; large ships berth in daylight and fair weather only, paradipport.gov.in) | weather_delay_days_monsoon 1.5: expected days per call lost to swell in the port's monsoon months (open-sea berths lose more than sheltered or river berths) - estimate for planning.
shore_equipment: 8 mobile harbour cranes of 100 t serving 4 bulk berths (the mechanised plant is for thermal-coal export)
handling_source: Paradip Port Authority, Know your port (paradipport.gov.in/know-your-port)

name: Haldia
notes: Panamax only part-laden; river/tidal port with shallow draft. LOA/beam now sourced (2026-09-22, previously blank): a port-agent reference sheet (samudramarine.com) gives inside-lock-gate berths (2,3,5,6,7) at LOA 230m/beam 32.26m; a separate search snippet put the coking-coal berth (4A) specifically at LOA 240m through the same lock - the two sources disagree by 10m on 4A, but neither changes feasibility here since both vessel classes actually allowed (Panamax 225m, Handymax 200m LOA) fit comfortably either way. The same source CONFIRMS Haldia's draft is genuinely republished monthly by the port (river port, real siltation-driven variation) and flags vessels drawing >8.5m fresh-water draft as restricted from NIGHT navigation specifically (not necessarily an absolute cap) - broadly consistent with, not contradicting, the existing 9.0m/1.0m figures, but still no exact monsoon reduction number found. CAVEAT: same PortWatch cross-check as before - Haldia's aggregate dry-bulk calls are flat across monsoon (+2.1%), no visible aggregate dip, see data/imf_portwatch_summary.csv. Still the port I'd trust this figure least at, of the 6.
ops_notes: Discharge rate = two harbour mobile cranes at berths 2 and 8 (Tariff Authority order KOPT-G195). Monsoon window not published; river drafts are declared daily - Jun-Sep assumed | weather_delay_days_monsoon 0.5: expected days per call lost to swell in the port's monsoon months (open-sea berths lose more than sheltered or river berths) - estimate for planning.
shore_equipment: Mobile harbour cranes at berths 2, 4B, 8, 13; 2 grab unloaders at mechanised berth 4A (3 mtpa coking coal)

name: Visakhapatnam
notes: VERIFIED: VGCB (Vizag General Cargo Berth, built for 200000 DWT) permissible LOA 300.0m, beam 50.0m, draft 18.1m (with 1.0m tidal allowance already factored). No monsoon reduction figure published for this berth in the source table, originally left at 0.0 pending confirmation. NOW CROSS-CHECKED against real IMF PortWatch daily port-call data (2019-2026, see data/imf_portwatch_summary.csv): dry-bulk port calls at Visakhapatnam run 12.7% HIGHER in Jun-Sep than the rest of the year, i.e. no aggregate monsoon slowdown is visible - consistent with (though not proof of) 0.0m being the right call for this specific, modern, tide-assisted outer-harbour berth. Source: Visakhapatnam Port Trust Marine Dept, 'Details of Restrictions and Allowable Drafts of Vessels in Inner/Outer Harbour', Outer Harbour Table.
ops_notes: 70,000 t/day rated for the VGCB outer-harbour berth (vpt.shipping.gov.in handling facilities). Monsoon window not published; matched to neighbouring Gangavaram's - no draft reduction is applied at this port | weather_delay_days_monsoon 0.5: expected days per call lost to swell in the port's monsoon months (open-sea berths lose more than sheltered or river berths) - estimate for planning.
shore_equipment: VGCB mechanised coking/steam coal terminal, 25,000 t/day minimum discharge, Capesize-capable

name: Gopalpur
notes: RESOLVED (2026-09-22): the old 14.2m figure and the 'conflicting sources' flag are both superseded. gopalpurports.in/.com are NOT live sites right now (both resolve to an unconfigured hosting panel), which is why earlier fetch attempts failed - the real source is Gopalpur's operator, Adani. Official BPTS/GPL/00 (w.e.f. 15-Feb-2025), Section B Berth Parameters table gives 3 berths: B-1 (LOA 300m, 145000 MT displacement, draft 14.5m), B-2 (same, PRIORITY FOR IMPORT COAL), B-3 (LOA 200m, 75000 MT, draft 14.5m). Port-level max vessel size is LOA 300m/beam 50m. Real monsoon period is 1-May to 30-Oct (port-specific, different from Gangavaram's 1-May-30-Nov) - the document notes permissible draft is 'promulgated monthly' i.e. genuinely seasonal, but doesn't state a reduction figure, so monsoon_draft_reduction_m is left at 0.0 (unknown, not zero-by-evidence) rather than guessed. CORRECTED vessel_classes_allowed: Post-Panamax (15.0m draft) does NOT fit under this port's real 14.5m cap and has been REMOVED (I had wrongly allowed it under the old, wrong 14.2m/290m figures - this is a genuine fix, not just an upgrade). Capesize (18.0m draft) still excluded. Source: adaniports.com, Gopalpur Port BPTS PDF.
ops_notes: Planning rate below the 32,000 t/day record (Wikipedia, Adani Gopalpur); monsoon window 1 May-30 Oct from the port operator (Adani Gopalpur BPTS/GPL/00, see notes) | weather_delay_days_monsoon 2.0: expected days per call lost to swell in the port's monsoon months (open-sea berths lose more than sheltered or river berths) - estimate for planning.
shore_equipment: Mobile harbour cranes with grabs; mechanised import berth (3,000 t/h system)
handling_source: Adani Ports, Gopalpur (adaniports.com/ports-and-terminals/gopalpur-port); J.M. Baxi newsletter

name: Sagar-Sandheads
notes: ADDED 2026-09-24 (named in the SIH26006 problem statement). Offshore transloading anchorage for Haldia/Kolkata: 40-50 m water at Sandheads so a laden Capesize can anchor (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haldia_Dock_Complex); Capesizes of 165k t cargo transloaded (maritimegateway.com). Draft set to 20 m because water depth is not the constraint. Flat charge = mother-vessel charge 7.345 US cents/GRT (~USD 6,800 for a Capesize) and per-tonne = 90% of the Rs 60.72/t coking-coal wharfage plus Rs 30.38/t at Haldia at ~Rs 96/USD (SMP Kolkata schedule of rates w.e.f. 31.10.2023). Wait range estimated.
ops_notes: Floating crane (Liebherr CBG 350) works at Sandheads about 8 months a year and moves to Kanika Sands in the monsoon (orissalinks.com), so transloading is treated as suspended Jun-Sep. Transloading rate, cost (USD 6-9/t for crane, barge and Haldia handling over ~63 nm) and the 2 extra days are estimates - not published. Rail onward from Haldia. | weather_delay_days_monsoon 2.0: expected days per call lost to swell in the port's monsoon months (open-sea berths lose more than sheltered or river berths) - estimate for planning.
shore_equipment: Floating cranes (e.g. MV Yugalraj, MV Viganraj) transload into barges for Haldia
